subject: Cross-region SLO carveout request: p50/p95 measurement parity
messages:
From: Samir Khan <skhan@evergreen-fin.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API SLOs — cross-region behavior and measurement

Hi Sofia / Ben,

Quick follow-up from yesterday's architecture review — we are aligning our SLAs with vendors and need one explicit ask: how does Redwood measure p50/p95 for cross-region traffic when requests exit our EU edge and are routed to a US region for inference? Our procurement team is asking for parity between EU and US measurement windows, and they want to understand if there is a temporary carveout or derating you can grant during our migration window (two-week canary).

Specifically we need:
- A written carveout option for spikes due to cross-region routing (UTC timestamps, 15-minute bursts).
- Confirmation of measurement window used for p95 calculation (sliding 5m? rolling epoch?).
- Any evidence you can share from previous cross-region canaries.

Can you send a short plan we can attach to the procurement packet?

Thanks,
Samir
VP Engineering, Evergreen Financial
[Attachment: migration-outline.docx (referenced)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <skhan@evergreen-fin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — cross-region behavior and measurement

Samir —

Thanks for the clear ask. I put together a short carveout proposal and attached a canary plan that we typically use for regional cutovers. High level:

1) Measurement windows: Redwood measures p50/p95 from the time the request enters our public edge to the final response emission (end-to-end). For contract commitments we report a rolling 1-minute aggregation feeding a 1-hour rolling epoch for SLA calculations (this is our standard for hosted API p50/p95).

2) Cross-region carveout: For customers performing an orchestrated migration that temporarily routes >10% traffic cross-region for up to 14 days, we can offer a "temporary regional routing carveout" that:
   - Excludes the first 10 minutes of a traffic shift event from SLA reporting (to avoid noisy cold-routing spikes).
   - Applies a transient smoothing grace that removes the top 0.5% of extreme notification spikes for the first 48 hours of the canary.

3) Evidence: attached is a sanitized canary-plan and a short evidence bundle (slo-evidence.zip) from a prior migration showing reduced P95 after smoothing.

Next steps: if procurement wants formal language, we will prepare an addendum that enumerates the exact carveout windows and triggers. Will that work for your packet?

Attaching: [Attachment: canary-plan.pdf (PDF, 240KB)], [Attachment: slo-evidence.zip (ZIP, 3.1MB)]

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Cross-region SLO carveout request — formal language and next steps

Samir / Procurement team —

Following our internal review, please find the formal carveout language we can include as an addendum to the Hosted API SLA. Key points below — full wording in the attached DocuSign draft: 

1) Measurement definition: p50/p95 are calculated end-to-end from ingress edge timestamp to response emission. Metrics are computed using a rolling 1-minute sample aggregation and evaluated across a rolling 1-hour epoch for SLA reporting.

2) Temporary regional routing carveout: Eligible when a customer triggers an orchestrated migration that routes >=10% of production traffic cross-region for a contiguous window up to 14 days. During the carveout window Redwood will:
   - Exclude the first 10 minutes after each routed-shift event from SLA calculations.
   - Apply a transient spike-trimming rule that excludes the top 0.5% of instantaneous samples for the first 48 hours of the carveout.
   - Provide daily CSV exports of the canary metrics and a short explanation of any excluded events.

3) Limits: Carveout may be requested once per 12-month period; Redwood reserves the right to deny requests that indicate prolonged cross-region routing beyond the 14-day window.

Attachments included for procurement: canary-plan.pdf, slo-evidence.zip, and a one-paragraph SLA addendum draft (DocuSign link below). If that looks good I'll get Legal to review and then route to DocuSign.
